key_insight: OmniRoam uses panoramic (360°) per-frame representations to generate long-horizon, globally consistent videos of a scene, enabling controllable "world wandering" that overcomes the limited field-of-view and short-horizon constraints of perspective video models.
problem_solved: Perspective video generators see only narrow views and struggle with completeness and global temporal/spatial consistency for long sequences; OmniRoam addresses incomplete scene coverage and lack of long-term coherence by operating on panoramic frames and explicit control signals.
method: Represent each timestep as a panoramic frame to provide full 360° scene coverage and stronger spatial continuity.
Train a generative backbone (e.g., transformer/diffusion-style) conditioned on camera trajectory/control inputs to produce long-horizon panoramic video while preserving global consistency.
Incorporate hierarchical memory/pose-conditioning and stitching mechanisms to maintain temporal coherence and accurate scene geometry across long sequences.
impact: Enables more complete and stable scene modeling for applications in virtual navigation, immersive media, simulation, and robotics; makes long-term controllable video synthesis practical for downstream tasks like data augmentation and exploration planning.

paper_title: OmniRoam: World Wandering via Long-Horizon Panoramic Video Generation
paper_authors: Yuheng Liu, Xin Lin, Xinke Li, Baihan Yang, Chen Wang
